name: AppToolbar
label: App toolbar
description: The bar along the top of an app’s page: the search, borderless icon controls, the AI button and a primary action, folding in steps as it narrows.

props.name: onSearch
props.description:
Opens the app's search, usually a CommandPalette. When given, the bar
starts with a search field, never narrower than a usable field, folded
to its icon when the bar is narrow.

props.name: searchLabel
props.description: The search field's prompt and accessible name. Default "Search or ask anything".

props.name: searchKeys
props.description:
The shortcut the search field shows, in the shortcut grammar. The
palette owns the key itself; this only draws it.

props.name: searchGlass
props.description:
Frosts the search field, in both its forms, for a bar that rides over a
busy ground (a map or a shader under the top of the page), so its prompt
reads over it. The other controls are ghost buttons and draw no fill.

props.name: actions
props.description:
The icon controls at the end, borderless: notifications, a calendar,
help, settings. On a narrow bar every one after the first moves into a
More menu, except those that open a panel or are links.

props.name: onChat
props.description:
Opens the app's AI chat. When given, an AiButton follows the icon
controls, folded to its icon when the bar is narrow.

props.name: chatLabel
props.description: The AI chat button's label. Default "Ask AI".

props.name: chatState
props.description:
What the agent behind the AI button is doing, in AgentStatus's
vocabulary, so the button can show it working.

props.name: chatExpanded
props.description: Whether the chat the AI button opens is open now, announced as the button's expanded state.

props.name: primaryAction
props.description:
The page's primary action, last in the row: a primary Button with a
leading icon, the AI button's size, folded to its icon when the bar is
narrow.

props.name: size
props.description:
The size of every control in the bar, on the row-control scale:
`default` is 40px, `compact` 32px. The search, the icon controls, the
AI button and the primary action always share one height.

props.name: linkComponent
toolbarLabel
props.description: The bar's accessible name. Default "App toolbar".

props.name: moreLabel
props.description: The More menu button's name, shown when the bar is narrow. Default "More".

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes on the bar

AppToolbarAction.description: One of the bar's icon controls, drawn as a borderless IconButton.

AppToolbarPrimaryAction.description: The bar's one primary action: a primary Button with a leading icon, last in the row.

LinkComponent.description: A component that renders a link in place of a plain `<a>`, such as a router's.

LinkComponentProps.description:
The props a link component receives: every anchor attribute, the ref, and
an `href` that is always a string. Next.js's `Link` takes these as they
are; a router whose link takes `to` instead needs a one-line adapter:
`({ href, ...props }) => <RouterLink to={href} {...props} />`.

Shortcut.description: A shortcut in the grammar above, such as `mod+k`, `shift+?` or `g i`.

keys.note: Tab moves through its controls in order; each control, the More menu among them, keeps its own keys.

alternatives.name: TableToolbar
alternatives.when: the bar sits over a table and holds its search, filters and view settings

alternatives.name: Toolbar
alternatives.when: the controls act on a canvas or a view and sit together in one pill
